Add real-time web search to 4 Bhudhi validation engine calls

The Erector validation engines currently call Bhudhi (Claude API) using only training data. For validation intelligence to be current and accurate — real industry health, real competitor landscape, real demand signals, real economic conditions — 4 specific Bhudhi calls must be upgraded to include the web_search_20250305 tool.

The Anthropic API natively supports web search via the tools parameter. No third-party integration is required. This prompt adds web search to exactly 4 calls and updates the response handler to process multi-block responses correctly.
THIS PROMPT TOUCHES ENGINE SERVICE FILES ONLY. No UI files, no schema, no migrations, no API route signatures are changed. The web search addition is internal to the Bhudhi call layer.
B — WHICH CALLS GET WEB SEARCH
Archetype profiles are structural system data. No real-time grounding needed.
Analyses user input text only. No market data required.
Must reflect current industry health, growth rates, platform shifts. Training data has a cutoff.
Needs current market size, demand trends, recent signals. Cannot be static.
Competitors change position, pricing, and product constantly. Must be current.
Economic conditions, inflation, regulatory environment, payment infrastructure are live data.
Synthesises from outputs of the above — no additional search needed.
Strategic synthesis from engine outputs — no new market data required.
Execution planning from archetype and path data.
Read every file listed below completely before writing a single line. The web search addition is surgical — reading first prevents overwriting existing logic.
Full registration pattern for all 10 Erector Bhudhi calls. Understand the existing fetch pattern, how prompts are built, how responses are consumed.
How calls route through the trigger router. How BhudhiLog is written. How fallbacks are triggered.
How analyze_industry is called and how its output is used. Note the exact variable names.
How analyze_market is called and how its output is used.
How identify_competitors is called and how its output is used.
How generate_economy_briefing is called and how its output is used.
D — THE CODE CHANGE (APPLY TO ALL 4 CALLS)
In each of the 4 Bhudhi calls (analyze_industry, analyze_market, identify_competitors, generate_economy_briefing), find the fetch call to the Anthropic API and add the tools parameter:
// BEFORE — existing call without web search

When web search is active, the API response contains multiple content blocks. The existing handler reads only data.content[0].text which will break. Replace the response extraction with a multi-block processor:
// BEFORE — reads only first block (breaks with web search)
// AFTER — processes all blocks, assembles full text output
// Extract text from all content blocks (web search returns tool_use + text)
// Log web search usage to BhudhiLog
For each of the 4 calls, add this instruction at the END of the existing system prompt string. Do not replace the existing prompt — append only:
// Append to existing prompt for analyze_industry:
IMPORTANT: Use web search to find current information about this industry before
responding. Search for: current state of [industry] in [country/region], recent
growth trends, market health in [year], and key players. Base your analysis on
what you find, not on potentially outdated training data. If search results
conflict with training data, prefer the search results.`
// Append to existing prompt for analyze_market:
IMPORTANT: Use web search to find current market data before responding. Search
for: current market size for [business model] in [country], demand trends in
[year], recent funding or growth signals in this space. Cite what you find.`
// Append to existing prompt for identify_competitors:
IMPORTANT: Use web search to identify real, currently operating competitors in
this space. Search for: top [business type] tools/platforms in [country/market]
[year], alternatives to [goal description], and market leaders in this category.
Return only real companies that exist today.`
// Append to existing prompt for generate_economy_briefing:
IMPORTANT: Use web search to ground your economy briefing in current conditions.
Search for: current economic conditions in [country] [year], business environment
[country] recent, payment infrastructure [country], and any recent regulatory
changes affecting [business type] businesses. Reflect what is actually happening
Add two nullable fields to the BhudhiLog write in all 4 upgraded calls. Do not change the BhudhiLog table schema — only the data written to it:
web_search_calls: searchesUsed, // how many searches were made
intelligence_grounded: searchesUsed > 0 // was real-time data used

If BhudhiLog does not have these columns yet, add them as nullable Int and Boolean in the schema: web_search_calls Int? and intelligence_grounded Boolean?. Run npx prisma migrate dev --name add_web_search_log.

Bhudhi automatically decides what to search based on the prompt. However, the prompt must contain enough context for it to build a useful search query. Ensure the following context variables are interpolated into each prompt before the web search instruction is appended:
Context variables that must be in the prompt
goal (rawGoal), businessModel, locationCountry, timeframe (current year derived from Date)
If these variables are already in the existing prompt, no change needed. If any are missing, add them to the existing prompt interpolation — do not rewrite the whole prompt.
Web search may fail or return no useful results. The existing deterministic fallback for each call must still work. Ensure the fallback path is not broken by the web search addition:
Continue with training data. Set intelligence_grounded = false in BhudhiLog. Do not crash.
Web search tool not available (API error)
Fall through to deterministic fallback as if Bhudhi call failed entirely. Log as fallback_used.
Response contains only tool_use blocks, no text block
Treat as Bhudhi failure. Use deterministic fallback. Log appropriately.
Anthropic API timeout with web search
Retry once without web search tool. If second attempt fails, use deterministic fallback.
